observations: Mobile steel frame for block moulding, painted yellow.
Single-cylinder diesel engine with a blue block and red fuel tank.
Belt and pulley drive system connecting the engine to the frame.
A separate metal mould with six cavities is positioned next to the machine in photo 2.
Manual levers for lifting the mould and pressing the blocks.
Watermark 'S.A.M NIG LTD' is present on all images.

claims.evidence: The design and construction are typical of locally fabricated industrial equipment in Nigeria.
The machine appears to be a manual-feed vibrating type; 'automated' usually implies a higher level of mechanical autonomy not evident in the photos.
The mould shown in photo 2 has six cavities, which does not align with a 'three' block capacity unless the seller is referring to a different configuration or block size.

risks.risk: The diesel engine may be non-functional or require significant repair.
risks.proof: A video of the engine starting and running smoothly.

risks.risk: The vibration mechanism (shaft and bearings) may be seized or damaged.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine vibrating under power.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring mechanical repair of the vibrator.

risks.risk: The mould shown may not be the correct fit for this specific machine frame.
risks.proof: A photo of the mould installed and aligned within the machine.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as the machine frame and engine only, without a functional mould.

proof_requests: Video of the engine running and the machine vibrating.
Photo of the mould installed in the machine.
Close-up photo of the engine's specification plate.
response.reason: The item is a standard locally-made block moulding machine. It can be priced based on its visible components, assuming the worst case for the engine and mechanical parts until proven otherwise.
